acceptance: The draft no longer says BenchBox ran different multi-warehouse code per platform; it describes the dead branch and the NULL defects accurately.
The post's numbers for current BenchBox behaviour come from complete-query timings recorded in `df-distinct-timing-confirmation`.
The front-matter placeholders noted in the draft (publication date, `post_number` 6 versus 7) are settled by the owner.
description:
Cross-repository gap; the work is in BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site, tracked here because the finding came from core and this session could not write to the site tracker. Draft PR #143 there (`drafts/benchbox-in-action/drafts/06-platform-specific-optimization-patterns.md`) says BenchBox picks the self-join for DataFusion in TPC-DS Q16 and Q95. The branch that did so was dead code in every release from v0.1.1 to v0.5.0 (it compared the platform with `"datafusion"`; the adapter reports `"DataFusion"`). The correction was posted as a comment on that PR on 2026-11-12; the draft text itself is unchanged. Core PR #4169 has since removed the branches, fixed NULL handling, and moved Q16, Q94 and Q95 to a min/max rule, so the post's description of current BenchBox behaviour is also out of date.

Expected: the draft states what BenchBox actually executed in February and executes now, and cites complete-query timings once `df-distinct-timing-confirmation` has them.

Guardrails: the thesis and publication date are the owner's editorial decisions. Do not publish isolated-step timings as if they were complete-query results. Site changes go by pull request in the site repository.
